score_rationale: Exceptional willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial B2B database market with at least 7 major vendors currently selling oil & gas and energy industry professional databases: Data Maelumat (102,525+ energy & utilities contacts), DataCaptive (verified oil & gas contacts), CampaignLake (272,000+ oil & gas industry contacts across upstream/midstream/downstream operations), Averick Media (45,000+ energy & utilities records), iInfoTanks (oil & gas email database), Blue Mail Media (energy industry email lists with 100% opt-in data), and BizProspex (oil & energy industry list at $200 entry price point). Commercial vendors report 85%+ deliverability rates with data updated every 3 months, indicating sustained high B2B demand and premium pricing models (most vendors require contact for enterprise quotes rather than transparent flat-file pricing). Five exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments with massive LTV justification: (1) Oil & gas software vendors (Petrel E&P software for subsurface modeling, Spotfire analytics, WellView production optimization, DrillingInfo/Enverus SaaS analytics at $10,000-$100,000/year subscriptions, SCADA systems for pipeline monitoring, reserves management software) selling mission-critical enterprise platforms to upstream producers, midstream pipeline operators, and downstream refiners at $50,000-$500,000/year contracts where one acquired customer generates 250×-2,500× ROI vs. $200 database cost; (2) Industrial equipment suppliers and oilfield services (Baker Hughes drilling equipment, Halliburton cementing and fracking services, Schlumberger wireline logging, NOV drilling rigs, Cameron blowout preventers, pressure pumping services, directional drilling, coiled tubing, well stimulation) selling capital equipment at $500,000-$50,000,000 per project plus ongoing maintenance contracts where one equipment sale justifies $10,000+ in prospecting and relationship development; (3) Industrial safety and compliance vendors (gas detection systems, flame detectors, personal protective equipment, confined space entry systems, fall protection, H2S monitoring, LEL sensors, SCBA respirators, FR clothing) selling to safety managers and HSE directors at oil refineries, drilling operations, and pipeline facilities with recurring $50,000-$500,000/year safety equipment and training budgets; (4) Environmental consulting and compliance firms (Phase I/II environmental site assessments for drilling sites, produced water treatment, spill response and remediation, air emissions monitoring, NPDES permitting, SPCC plans, tank integrity testing) billing $10,000-$500,000 per project to ensure regulatory compliance with EPA, state oil & gas commissions, and BLM regulations; and (5) Financial services specialized for energy sector (oil & gas investment banks, reserve-based lending, hedging and derivatives for commodity price risk, project finance for pipeline construction, midstream infrastructure financing, royalty trust management) where one client relationship generates $100,000-$5,000,000 in annual fees. Massive total addressable market: U.S. oil & gas industry employs 1.2+ million workers across 10,000+ exploration & production companies, 2,500+ midstream pipeline operators, 150+ refineries, 5,000+ oilfield services companies, plus renewable energy sector adding 500,000+ jobs in solar, wind, and clean energy (per Bureau of Labor Statistics 2026 data), creating combined 50,000-100,000 decision-maker contacts (petroleum engineers, drilling managers, production supervisors, facilities managers, procurement directors, operations VPs, HSE managers). Partial public data availability: some states with significant oil & gas operations maintain operator registries (Texas Railroad Commission maintains operator list for O&G permits, North Dakota Industrial Commission Oil & Gas Division, Oklahoma Corporation Commission, Colorado ECMC, Wyoming Oil & Gas Conservation Commission, New Mexico EMNRD Oil Conservation Division, Louisiana DNR Office of Conservation) with business names, operator numbers, and contact information as public records under FOIA; however engineering firm directories, refinery operator lists, and pipeline company databases are typically compiled from industry associations (American Petroleum Institute, Interstate Natural Gas Association of America, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers) and business registries rather than centralized public licensing. Engineering lift is moderate-to-high: aggregate state oil & gas operator registries, cross-reference with EPA facility databases (TRI toxic release facilities, NPDES permit holders for refineries and chemical plants), scrape industry association member directories, parse SEC filings for publicly traded E&P companies and pipeline operators, geocode facility locations, classify by sector (upstream/midstream/downstream/oilfield services/renewable), normalize job titles and company hierarchies, deduplicate multi-state operators. No affordable flat-file competitor exists below $200 on Gumroad — all existing vendors (7+ identified) use enterprise pricing models requiring sales contact for quotes, with traditional pattern of $0.20-$0.75 per contact for specialized industrial B2B lists, making a $149-$199 one-time CSV deliver 60-90% cost savings vs. traditional per-contact pricing for 100K+ records. Score is 8 due to: (a) exceptionally strong validated commercial vendor ecosystem with 7+ active vendors and sustained demand despite premium/enterprise pricing, (b) ultra-high buyer LTV across all five segments (software $50K-$500K/year, equipment sales $500K-$50M per project, safety/compliance $50K-$500K/year recurring, environmental consulting $10K-$500K per project, financial services $100K-$5M/year fees) where one customer acquisition justifies 50×-25,000× database cost, (c) large and high-value TAM (50K-100K decision-makers across 18,000+ companies in capital-intensive industry), (d) partial public data availability through state regulatory agencies combined with industry association directories, (e) absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives despite strong market demand, and (f) multiple proven high-value buyer verticals (software, equipment, safety, environmental, finance) creating diversified revenue opportunity. Score not higher than 8 due to: (a) fragmented data sources requiring aggregation across state agencies, EPA databases, SEC filings, and industry associations rather than single centralized public registry, (b) moderate-to-high engineering complexity to normalize company hierarchies and deduplicate multi-state operators, and (c) partial reliance on scraped industry directories rather than 100% government-maintained public records, though state operator registries and EPA facility data provide strong foundational dataset.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all identifiable oil & gas companies, energy industry professionals, and renewable energy operators extracted from state oil & gas commission operator registries (Texas RRC, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Colorado, Wyoming, New Mexico, Louisiana), EPA facility databases (TRI toxic release facilities, NPDES refineries), industry association member directories (API, INGAA, AFPM), and SEC filings for publicly traded energy companies. Each record includes company legal name, DBA/trade name, primary contact name and title (CEO, operations manager, drilling supervisor, facilities director, procurement VP, HSE manager where publicly listed), business mailing address, facility/headquarters location, phone, email (where public in regulatory filings), operator number or facility ID, sector classification (upstream E&P, midstream pipelines, downstream refining, oilfield services, renewable energy), state(s) of operation, and facility type (drilling rig, production facility, refinery, pipeline terminal, wind farm, solar installation). As of 2026, approximately 10,000+ exploration & production companies, 2,500+ midstream operators, 150+ refineries, 5,000+ oilfield services firms, plus 3,000+ renewable energy companies (solar installers, wind farm operators, clean energy developers), for combined 20,000+ energy industry businesses with 50,000-100,000 decision-maker contacts. Five exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) Oil & gas software vendors (Petrel subsurface modeling, Enverus/DrillingInfo analytics at $10K-$100K/year, WellView production optimization, SCADA pipeline monitoring, reserves management platforms) selling mission-critical enterprise software at $50K-$500K/year subscriptions where one acquired customer = 250×-2,500× database cost ROI; (2) Industrial equipment suppliers (Baker Hughes, Halliburton, Schlumberger oilfield services, NOV drilling rigs at $500K-$50M per rig, Cameron blowout preventers, pressure pumping, directional drilling, wireline logging) where one equipment sale justifies $10K+ prospecting spend; (3) Safety & compliance vendors (gas detection systems, flame detectors, PPE, H2S monitors, FR clothing, SCBA respirators) selling to HSE managers with $50K-$500K/year recurring safety budgets; (4) Environmental consulting firms (Phase I/II site assessments, produced water treatment, spill remediation, air emissions monitoring, NPDES permitting) billing $10K-$500K per compliance project; (5) Energy-specialized financial services (reserve-based lending, commodity hedging, project finance for $100M+ pipeline construction, royalty trust management) generating $100K-$5M/year in fees per client relationship. A one-time $149-$199 CSV undercuts traditional B2B energy database vendors (7+ vendors identified requiring enterprise sales contact for quotes, typical $0.20-$0.75/contact = $10K-$75K for 100K records) while delivering complete TAM across upstream/midstream/downstream/services/renewables for software vendors, equipment suppliers, safety providers, environmental consultants, and financial services targeting capital-intensive energy sector with ultra-high contract values.

data_wanted: State oil & gas regulatory agencies maintain operator registries as public records: Texas Railroad Commission (rrc.texas.gov) maintains comprehensive operator database with all companies holding drilling permits or operating leases in Texas (largest U.S. oil producer), searchable by operator name or operator number with business entity, mailing address, and responsible party contact information; North Dakota Industrial Commission Oil & Gas Division maintains operator list for Bakken shale producers; Oklahoma Corporation Commission Oil & Gas Conservation Division; Colorado Energy & Carbon Management Commission; Wyoming Oil & Gas Conservation Commission; New Mexico Energy, Minerals & Natural Resources Department Oil Conservation Division; Louisiana Department of Natural Resources Office of Conservation. EPA facility databases provide refinery and chemical plant data: Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) includes all petroleum refineries and petrochemical plants reporting toxic chemical releases with facility name, parent company, facility address, contacts, and NAICS codes; NPDES permit database includes refineries, gas processing plants, and terminals with wastewater discharge permits listing facility operators and contact info. Industry association member directories (publicly accessible): American Petroleum Institute members list, Interstate Natural Gas Association of America pipeline operator members, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers refinery member directory. SEC EDGAR filings for publicly traded E&P companies, midstream MLPs, and integrated majors (ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, Pioneer Natural Resources, Occidental Petroleum, Kinder Morgan pipelines, Energy Transfer Partners, Williams Companies) with executive contacts and operational facility locations disclosed in 10-K annual reports. Renewable energy facility databases: EIA electricity generator database includes all utility-scale wind farms and solar installations with owner/operator names and facility details. Target fields per record: Company legal name and DBA, primary contact name and title (CEO, COO, VP Operations, Drilling Manager, Production Superintendent, Facilities Manager, Procurement Director, HSE Manager where publicly disclosed in regulatory filings), business mailing address, headquarters and facility locations, phone number, email (where public), operator number or facility ID, sector (upstream E&P, midstream pipeline/storage, downstream refining/marketing, oilfield services - drilling/cementing/fracking, renewable - solar/wind), commodities (crude oil, natural gas, NGLs, refined products, renewable power), state(s) of operation, facility type and count (producing wells, drilling rigs, refineries, pipeline terminals, compressor stations, wind turbines, solar arrays), parent company and corporate hierarchy for subsidiaries. Target all active operators across upstream (E&P producers and drillers), midstream (pipeline companies, storage terminals, gas processing plants), downstream (refineries, petrochemical plants, fuel distribution), oilfield services (drilling contractors, cementing, pressure pumping, wireline), and renewable energy (utility-scale solar and wind). Approximately 10,000+ E&P operators, 2,500+ midstream companies, 150 refineries (130+ operating petroleum refineries per EIA), 5,000+ oilfield services firms, 3,000+ renewable energy project operators, for combined 20,000-25,000 total companies generating 50,000-100,000 decision-maker contact records. Target output: 75,000+ rows minimum (many individuals hold multiple titles, creating separate contact records per decision-maker). Data is substantially public: state oil & gas operator registries are public records under state open records laws and FOIA, EPA facility databases are federally mandated public disclosures, SEC filings are public, and industry association directories are published for member visibility — no authentication barriers or paywalls for core regulatory data, though executive contact enrichment may require LinkedIn scraping or business directory lookups to supplement regulatory filings.
